Good evening. Have you been to a Japanese restaurant before?
Good evening. Yes, many times. In Brazil we eat a lot of Japanese food.
Ah, São Paulo, of course. Then you know more than most of my customers.
To start, two miso soups, please.
Of course. And for the main? The sushi set is very popular this evening.
Is the fish raw in the set? My son is eight.
It is, yes. For the little ones I would suggest the chicken katsu.
Then chicken katsu for the children. For me the grilled salmon — I prefer it, because it is not spicy.
A good choice. Would you like anything else with that at all?
Sorry, I don't understand. Can you say that again, more slowly?
Sorry. Anything more? Rice? Vegetables?
Extra rice, please. And a fork for the children — they cannot use chopsticks yet. Try the salmon with lemon, it is delicious like that.
With lemon? I will tell the kitchen. Thank you — I learn something every day.
Is the fish raw or cooked?

Good evening, everybody. Before you order, let me tell you about tonight, because three things are not on the menu. The first is a salmon that arrived this morning, and the chef serves it grilled with lemon and rice. It is not spicy at all, so it is good for children too. The second is a cold noodle dish with vegetables, and it is the only one on the menu that is completely vegetarian tonight. And the third is a small sushi set for people who do not want raw fish: everything in it is cooked, and it is the one I recommend for families. About the spicy ramen on the menu: it is genuinely very spicy, so please ask me before you order it for a child. Forks are always available, and nobody has to use chopsticks. Thank you.

Hello, this is the Sakura restaurant, returning your call about Saturday evening. We have a table for four at half past seven, next to the window, as you asked. Two things about what you told us on the telephone. First, the nut allergy: I spoke to the chef this morning, and the sushi, the salmon and the chicken katsu have no nuts at all. The only dish with nuts is the cold noodle one, so we simply will not bring it near your table. Second, you asked if the children can have something not raw. Yes, of course: we do a small cooked set for children, with rice, and it is nine pounds. If your son prefers, the chicken katsu is also cooked, and most children choose that one. Forks come with every table, so please do not worry about the chopsticks. See you on Saturday at half past seven.
Good evening. Two miso soups to start, please. Is the fish raw? I prefer the grilled salmon, because it is not spicy. And a fork for the children, please. Thank you very much.
